title: Where Does the Sun’s Wind Meet Earth?

segments.text: Did you know the Sun’s wind meets Earth’s magnetosphere?
The magnetosphere is the space region where Earth’s magnetic field dominates.
It sits above the ionosphere, extending thousands of kilometres.
The magnetosphere keeps harmful charged particles from reaching the air.
The magnetopause marks where the Sun’s wind pressure balances Earth’s magnetic pressure.
Ahead of that is the bow shock, where the wind slows abruptly.
Inside, the plasmasphere forms a donut‑shaped cloud of low‑energy particles.
These particles orbit Earth and drift along field lines.
Some drift westward, others eastward, creating a ring current.
That current weakens the field at the surface.
The magnetosphere also blocks most cosmic rays.
The Sun’s wind meets Earth’s shield at the magnetopause.
